_note: TEMPLATE. The real file (opencode.json, next to this one) is GENERATED by mango-code.ps1 at every start by replacing the {{placeholders}} with the values of the running model. Don't edit opencode.json by hand: it gets rewritten. Everything else here is edited. The placeholders: TOQ-v1 model name, 122880 EFFECTIVE context in tokens, 15360 generation ceiling, C:\Test\dist launcher folder with doubled backslashes (JSON), toq the key (3.6 / 3.8).
_why_generated: The context changes with the model: 128k on the 3.6 MoE, 80k on the dense 3.8. If it were written by hand in opencode.json it would become a SECOND place where that number lives and sooner or later it would lie. The single source is mango-models.json.
_zero_cloud: share disabled + autoupdate false: mango-code talks to no server other than our own llama-server and our MCPs.
_small_model: Points to the SAME provider/model as the running one. opencode uses small_model for small jobs (session title, summaries): on a local model it must be mango/local (otherwise it looks for a cloud provider and the session starts with an authentication error); on a cloud model there is no reason to pay for a second one for the same small jobs.

mango.name: mango-code
mango._baseURL: GENERATED. Normally http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1, but with mango-code -Remote <ip> it becomes the address of the PC that keeps the model running: it is the only difference between running the model on this PC and using it from another PC on the wifi. Written by hand in here it would be the second place where that address lives.
mango._options: apiKey is fake but MUST be there: the OpenAI-compatible client refuses to start without it. timeout false and headerTimeout 15 min are not paranoia: with a local model on an RTX 3060 Ti + GTX 1080 + GTX 1660 SUPER a 50k-token prefill can take two minutes before the first byte, and the defaults (30-60 s) would cut the request exactly on long contexts, that is when it is needed.

local.name: TOQ-v1
local._modalities: GENERATED: [text, image] if the model has the mmproj in mango-models.json, [text] for a text-only model. REQUIRED, and not a duplicate of attachment. MEASURED by capturing the real request: without this line, when a tool returns an image (chrome-devtools_take_screenshot) opencode does NOT send it to the model - in its place it inserts a user message saying 'ERROR: Cannot read image (this model does not support image input). Inform the user.' From there the model answered 'I cannot see screenshots' and fell back on the accessibility tree, which costs four times as much. The reason is in provider.ts: capabilities.input.image is computed from modalities.input.includes('image'), while 'attachment' ends up in another field that this check does not look at. VL models with their --mmproj really do handle images.
local._interleaved: llama-server extracts the <think> into reasoning_content (--reasoning-format, default deepseek). Telling opencode this, the thinking ends up in its panel instead of dirtying the answer.
local._cost: Really zero: nobody counts the electricity. It is needed because opencode sums the costs per session and without this field it would show NaN.
local._attachment: GENERATED like modalities: true only if the engine loads an --mmproj.
local._variants: No variants: the model ALWAYS reasons, and without variants the web UI does not show the selector next to the model. low/medium/high are the ones opencode adds by itself to openai-compatible providers (reasoningEffort, which llama-server ignores). The session title is generated without thinking all the same: the agent does it in smallOptions (transform.ts), only for the mango provider.

openrouter.name: openrouter

unused/unused.name: n/a
unused/unused._modalities: GENERATED from the 'image' block of the cloud model in mango-models.json. REQUIRED, not a duplicate of 'attachment': provider.ts computes capabilities.input.image from modalities.input.includes('image'), while 'attachment' ends up in another field that this check does not look at. If the model accepts images but here it stayed [text], opencode does NOT send the image to the model and in its place inserts 'ERROR: Cannot read image (this model does not support image input). Inform the user.'

openrouter._openrouter: CLOUD provider, not local: unlike 'mango' here the apiKey is REAL (from mango-secrets.json, gitignored) and baseURL is openrouter.ai. Active only if the running model in mango-models.json has a 'cloud' block - otherwise it stays declared but unused. The model key under 'models' MUST be the exact id OpenRouter expects (it contains '/': opencode accepts it, it splits only on the first slash to separate provider and model).

_screenshot_tool: GENERATED: false for a text-only model, which cannot look at a screenshot.
_tools_chrome: MEASURED by capturing the real request to the model: the tool definitions weighed 46481 characters against the 22645 of the system prompt - the tools are twice the instructions, and they are paid at EVERY turn in prefill, which for a local model is the bottleneck. chrome-devtools alone was 25429 over 29 tools. Here the eight that are duplicates or will never be used are dropped: lighthouse and heapsnapshot (profiling, not navigation), drag/hover/type_text (covered by click, fill and press_key), upload_file (needs a real file picker), get_console_message (list_console_messages already exists), select_page (with pageIdRouting on every call already carries its pageId). The performance and emulation categories are not here: mango-chrome-mcp.mjs turns them off with --no-category-*, that is before opencode even sees them.
_tools: task false = no subagents: a local 27-35B with a single slot has nothing to gain by splitting itself, and every subagent is another prefill to pay. websearch false because opencode's built-in goes through an external provider: the search is done by OUR MCP (mcp__web-search__*), which runs in-house. webfetch stays on: it makes the HTTP request directly, with no intermediaries.
_permission: Full autonomy: local machine, personal use, and a model that stops to ask for every write is unusable. It is DECLARED item by item instead of being a single flag: you see what is being granted, and removing a permission is one line.
_compaction: prune stays false (the default): it replaces old tool outputs once they pass ~40k tokens, which changes the old part of the conversation and makes the engine re-read everything after it (tens of thousands of tokens, again every ~20k). The engine cache comes first; when the context is full, auto compaction summarizes once.
_skills: The 14 skills stay WHERE THEY ARE (mango-plugin\skills), neither copied nor linked: opencode reads them from their place. The format is SKILL.md. They stay ISOLATED: they are in this config, which lives only inside mango-code, so the user's normal opencode does not see them.
_web_instructions: How to look at a web page depends on the model of the request: MANGO-web-images.md for one that sees images (pages looked at with the screenshot), MANGO-web-text.md for a text-only one (pages looked at with the snapshot). The mango-discipline plugin adds them to the system prompt, because in the app one process serves several models.
_role_instructions: Empty outside -Team. In -Team it points to MANGO-manager.md or MANGO-dev.md: that is where each model learns that it is not alone, what its role is, and how it behaves with the other (see mango-team.js for the mechanism).
_plugin: Normally empty: the plugins in opencode-home\plugin\ load by themselves because they are in the 'plugin' folder NEXT TO this file (OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR). It is filled ONLY for the -Team manager, which lives in a different config folder (runtime\opencode-manager\) precisely to have a model of its own: there that automatic scan does not see it, so mango-code.ps1 puts it explicitly, with absolute paths. It stays empty for the dev: loading it this way too would be the same plugin twice.
_timeout_30s: A short timeout, not the 120000 ms default: the stdio channel between opencode and the MCP server can die silently (server and browser alive, but opencode sends and the server receives NOTHING). The server cannot notice - nothing arrives for it to notice - so the only defense is for the client to give up QUICKLY: with a long timeout every call after the break costs minutes. At 30 s the model understands within two calls that something is wrong. The server's protocolTimeout is 20 s, that is BELOW this: the order of the two numbers is the rule, and it must be kept.
_mcp: Three servers: web search (mango-websearch-mcp.js), browser (mango-chrome-mcp.mjs) and Word/Excel/PowerPoint/PDF documents. The tools that are not needed are cut with 'tools': each one weighs in the prefill at every turn.
_why_node_not_npx: chrome-devtools-mcp is launched with `node` on the mango-chrome-mcp.mjs wrapper (which then loads Google's server from the local node_modules), NOT with `npx -y ...@latest`. The wrapper decides WHICH Chrome to attach to - mango-code's Chrome on 9333, the real profile via chrome://inspect (the one with your logins), or a new visible and persistent one: the long explanation is at the top of that file. Two reasons, and the first is a real bug: on Windows `npx` goes through a .cmd shim, so opencode opens a cmd.exe that INHERITS our console; when that cmd.exe exits it puts the console back in cooked mode and opencode's TUI stops receiving keys - a screen that draws perfectly but in which nothing can be typed. With `node` directly no cmd.exe is born. The second reason is consistency with the ethos: `@latest` made a round trip on the network at EVERY start, and --no-usage-statistics + --no-performance-crux turn off Google telemetry and the CrUX API calls. The dependency is in package.json: `npm install` in the launcher folder installs it.
